land.text: the Dutch East India Company's Taiwan, ruled 'from Fort Zeelandia (Tayouan)'; the Dutch 'ended ... rule over Taiwan' on 1 February 1662

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws the Zheng regime's Taiwan inside its 'Southern Ming' row (shape southern-ming_1662, 40,939 km2, 1662-1672; the 1673-1682 shapes add the Three Feudatories); see notes.

land.text: Taiwan and Penghu: 'Taiwan was then formally annexed in April 1684' as Taiwan Prefecture of Fujian

successors.note: The surrender was 5 September 1683 (second petition reached Penghu); Shi Lang arrived in Taiwan on 5 October 1683; annexation April 1684.

capitals.name: Anping (Fort Zeelandia, present-day Tainan), with the Eastern Capital (Dongdu) at Chikan
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: Anping (present-day Tainan)'; 'On 29 May 1662, Chikan was renamed to "Ming Eastern Capital" (Dongdu Mingjing)'; Koxinga renamed Fort Zeelandia to Anping and Provintia to Chikan. Anping was in Dutch hands until February 1662.

rulers.name: Zheng Keshuang
rulers.note: Infobox: 1681-1683; his surrender petition reached Penghu on 5 September 1683.

union.text: Tainan: Fort Provintia (Chikan) and the landing at Tayouan

correction.text: Koxinga's holdings in 1661: the Tainan beachhead, Penghu, Kinmen and Xiamen

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no Tungning row. The beachhead at Tainan (Fort Provintia surrendered on 4 April 1661; Fort Zeelandia was besieged from 7 April), Penghu (garrison left on 30 March), and the mainland-coast bases Kinmen and Xiamen the fleet sailed from on 23 March. The infobox gives no area.

union.text: the western plain of Taiwan from the southern tip to Hsinchu

correction.text: Taiwan's western plain with Penghu, Kinmen and Xiamen until the Qing took Xiamen and Kinmen in November 1663

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the Dutch surrender (terms finalised 1 February 1662, garrison out on 9 February) the Zheng hold the Dutch Taiwan; the Tungning page says Han settlement spread 'across the southwest plain to the southern tip of the island, and as far north as modern Hsinchu'. A polygon ring (119.8-121.1 E, 21.8-24.95 N) cut to the island stands for the western plain; the Dutch still hold Keelung to 1668. About 20,000 km2 against no infobox area.

New keyframe: after the loss of Xiamen and Kinmen ('In 1663 the Dutch helped the Qing capture Zheng bases in Xiamen and Kinmen in November'; the Zheng forces 'fully left the mainland coast in spring 1664') the kingdom is Taiwan's western plain and Penghu.

correction.text: Taiwan's western plain, Keelung and Penghu

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Keelung joins when the Dutch, who 'held out at Keelung until 1668', withdraw from Taiwan; the pages do not say the Zheng took it, so this is a reading (confidence 1 in the ledger).

correction.text: Taiwan with the Fujian-Guangdong coast from Xiamen to Chaozhou, 1674-1676

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Fujian coast regained during the Revolt of the Three Feudatories: Zheng Jing 'recaptured Xiamen' in 1674 and took Quanzhou and Zhangzhou; Chaozhou's commander defected in 1675. Quanzhou fell back to the Qing on 12 March 1677 and Zhangzhou on 5 April 1677, but Haicheng was retaken in August 1677; the mainland war ended on 10 April 1680. The shape holds to 1676 and the 1677-1679 shape keeps Xiamen, Haicheng and Chaozhou.

correction.text: Taiwan with Xiamen, Haicheng and Chaozhou, 1677-1679

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Quanzhou lost 12 March 1677 and Zhangzhou 5 April 1677, Haicheng retaken in August 1677; the page does not say what happened to Chaozhou, so it is kept to the end of the mainland war (April 1680) as a reading.
New keyframe: after the mainland war ends (10 April 1680) Taiwan, Keelung and Penghu remain until the Qing capture Penghu on 18 July 1683 and Zheng Keshuang surrenders (5 September 1683).

region.text: the Tainan beachhead, Penghu, Kinmen and Xiamen

ledger.note: 1661: Koxinga's fleet lands on Taiwan. 'On 23 March 1661, Koxinga's forces set sail from Kinmen (Quemoy)'; the fleet 'arrived at Tayouan on 2 April'; 'On 4 April, Fort Provintia surrendered to the Zheng forces.' The infobox dates the kingdom's establishment to 1 February 1662 (the Dutch surrender); the dossier starts with the landing because the Zheng regime holds ground from April 1661.

7 April 1661: the siege of Fort Zeelandia begins. 'On April 7, Koxinga's army surrounded Fort Zeelandia' (Siege page infobox: March 30, 1661 - February 1, 1662); Coyett held it 'with 1,733 people', Valentyn Fort Provintia with 140 soldiers.

1 February 1662: the Dutch surrender. 'Coyett negotiated terms of surrender, a process that was finalized on February 1'; 'On the 9th of February, the remaining Dutch East India Company personnel left Taiwan' (the Tungning page dates the surrender itself to 12 January 1662).

region.text: the Dutch Taiwan: the western plain from Fort Zeelandia northwards, up to Hsinchu

ledger.note: February 1662: Taiwan passes from the Dutch East India Company to the Zheng. The war 'ended the Dutch East India Company's rule over Taiwan'; the Dutch 'held out at Keelung until 1668'. The extent is the Tungning page's Han settlement 'as far north as modern Hsinchu'.

region.text: Xiamen and Kinmen, the Zheng bases on the Fujian coast

ledger.note: November 1663: the Qing, helped by the Dutch, take Xiamen and Kinmen. 'In 1663 the Dutch helped the Qing capture Zheng bases in Xiamen and Kinmen in November'; the Zheng 'fully left the mainland coast in spring 1664'.

region.text: Keelung, the last Dutch holding on Taiwan

ledger.note: 1668: the Dutch leave Keelung. 'The Dutch held out at Keelung until 1668, then withdrew from Taiwan altogether'; the pages do not say who took Keelung, so the gain to the Zheng is a bridging reading. The Dutch Formosa page (second page, see the dutch-formosa dossier) adds that 'the Dutch retook the northern fortress at Keelung in 1664', which would mean the Zheng held Keelung 1662-1664; this dossier follows the Tungning and Siege pages ('held out at Keelung until 1668').

1674: Zheng Jing joins the Revolt of the Three Feudatories. 'In 1674 Zheng Jing recaptured Xiamen' and took Quanzhou and Zhangzhou from the Qing (Tungning page); Zhangzhou was 'captured by Zheng in 1674'.
1675: Chaozhou comes over. 'the Chaozhou commander, Liu Jingzhong, defected to Zheng in 1675'; the page does not say Zheng lost it, and the end of the mainland war in 1680 is the bridge.
12 March 1677: Quanzhou 'lost to the Qing on 12 March 1677'.
5 April 1677: Zhangzhou 'lost to the Qing on 5 April 1677'.
August 1677: 'Haicheng was retaken by Zheng in August 1677'; the town is placed in the Zhangzhou district by the researcher.

region.text: Xiamen and the remaining mainland holdings

ledger.note: 10 April 1680: the war on the mainland ends. 'the Zheng war on the mainland ended on 10 April 1680'; Xiamen 'abandoned in 1680'. Haicheng and Chaozhou are bridged (confidence 2): the page gives no separate date.
18 July 1683: the Qing take Penghu. 'The Qing captured Penghu on 18 July' after the Battle of Penghu (10-16 July 1683); Shi Lang commanded the Qing fleet and Liu Guoxuan the Tungning forces.

region.text: Taiwan: the western plain and Keelung

ledger.note: 5 September 1683: Zheng Keshuang surrenders Taiwan. Infobox 'Surrender to the Qing: 5 September 1683' (the second petition reached Penghu); Shi Lang reached Taiwan on 5 October 1683 and 'Taiwan was then formally annexed in April 1684' (Taiwan under Qing rule page).

wars.name: Siege of Fort Zeelandia
wars.outcome: Ming loyalists' victory: the Dutch East India Company lost Taiwan on 1 February 1662, except Keelung (held to 1668).

wars.name: Qing capture of Xiamen and Kinmen
wars.outcome: The Qing, with Dutch help, took the Zheng bases in November 1663; the Zheng left the mainland coast by spring 1664.
wars.note: Not an article of its own among the pages opened; the Tungning page gives the dates.

wars.name: Zheng campaigns in the Revolt of the Three Feudatories
wars.outcome: Zheng Jing retook Xiamen, Quanzhou and Zhangzhou in 1674; the tide turned after 1676-1677 and the mainland war ended on 10 April 1680.
wars.note: The Revolt of the Three Feudatories article itself was not opened.

wars.name: Battle of Penghu
wars.outcome: Qing victory: Penghu captured on 18 July 1683 and Zheng Keshuang's capitulation of Taiwan followed.

certainty.note: Han settlement on Taiwan's plains had no fixed frontier with aboriginal land (the Qing later required permits beyond the Dajia River); the island coast and the mainland towns are known places, drawn as radii.

notes:
Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-24 from four pages. Cliopatria has no Tungning row, but its 'Southern Ming' row (ea-07) carries the Zheng regime's land: southern-ming_1662 (1662-1672, a 40,939 km2 patch in Taiwan, 120.0-122.0 E, 21.95-25.29 N) and the 1673-1682 shapes (which add the Three Feudatories' south China). Whoever writes the southern-ming dossier should treat Taiwan 1662-1683 as this dossier's land (the Southern Ming itself ended with the Yongli Emperor's death in 1662, which the Tungning page notes Zheng Jing ignored: he 'treated the deceased Yongli Emperor as though he were still alive'). This dossier's own Taiwan shape is about half the island (the western plain); Cliopatria's 40,939 km2 is larger than the island's land, so ea-07's shape is the whole island.

Not settled: (1) start: the infobox 'Established: 1 February 1662' against the landing of April 1661 (this dossier starts in April 1661, fixed by Fort Provintia's surrender on 4 April); the Tungning page puts the Dutch surrender on 12 January 1662, the siege page says the terms were finalised on 1 February; (2) who took Keelung in 1668 (page silent: confidence 1); (3) the fate of Chaozhou after 1675 and of Haicheng in 1680; (4) the Penghu islands between 1661 and 1683 beyond the 30 March 1661 garrison; (5) the Tungning page gives no area; the Tamsui and east-coast situation is not on the pages; (6) the Revolt of the Three Feudatories and the Xiamen 1663 fighting have no article opened; (7) the ruler Koxinga's title 'Prince of Yanping' is not on the extract and was not used; (8) family 'china-division' is a suggestion. Gazetteer: all names are known, but the Penghu admin1 resolves to no cells (the islands are smaller than the 253 km2 grid cells), so Penghu's capture on 18 July 1683 cannot be drawn on this grid; Kinmen resolves to one cell.
